about: Pedro Pascal Laughing Then Crying is a two-panel webcam still of the actor in a gray T-shirt: on top he is cackling with his head thrown back, and on the bottom the same laugh has collapsed into an open-mouthed sob, eyebrows bunched in anguish. The format captures how fast a joke can turn on you. The top panel is the moment something seems hilarious, and the bottom panel is the moment you realize it is about you, or that the funny thing has a very sad side.
origin: The footage is from a virtual play reading Pascal took part in during 2020, recorded over video call. In early 2021 the laughing-to-crying clip spread on TikTok as a reaction, and the two stills became a popular image template.
usage:
The top box is the funny setup: what you are laughing at. The bottom box is the twist that makes you cry: the realization that it applies to you, or the sad consequence hiding behind it.

The sharper the turn from top to bottom, the better. Roasts that turn out to be personal, deadlines that are closer than you thought, and nostalgic jokes about how old everyone is are the classic uses. Keep the bottom line short so the reveal hits fast.

watching someone fail the exam question
